lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Down the lane, behind a gate hanging by one hinge, a terrace waits under a tangle of ivy. Grandma's last letter said it misses her.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: It does look lonely. Four wobbly tables, a piano under a bedsheet, and a fountain that gave up years ago.

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: This is where I did my best baking, dear. Warm evenings, fairy lights, everyone with a second helping they swore they didn't want.

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: The shop feeds the street. The terrace is where the street sits down and stays a while. Both matter.

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: Bring more hens, more sugar and a bigger oven. And don't let anyone tell you cake is a frivolous thing to be good at.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You find the broom behind the gate. Time to sweep.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A woman with a sketchbook under one arm stops at the freshly wiped tables and does a slow lap, like a judge at a county fair.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Hm. Good bones. Honestly, great bones. Nobody has loved this place properly in a long time.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: I'm Priya. I design wedding cakes, and I've been looking for somewhere with this much character. And, apparently, this many pigeons.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Your gran once made me a lemon cupcake when I'd failed my first apprenticeship. I still think about it. The cupcake, and the kindness.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Cupcakes, cake slices, the occasional truffle. If you can make those, I'll be your most opinionated customer.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Priya is now a regular.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: An elderly man in a flat cap leans over the new herb planters with the air of someone inspecting a rival's work.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Rosemary's too close to the mint. Mint takes over. Mint always takes over. Nobody listens.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Bramble. I keep the allotment behind the church. Forty years of tomatoes, and I'll thank you not to ask about the slugs.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Your grandmother swapped me a tin of oat cookies for a bag of runner beans every autumn. Best trade I ever made.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: I'll take cookies, if you've got them. And eggs, by the carton. My hens have gone on strike.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Mr. Bramble is now a regular.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The old piano gives one clear note, then a second. Someone has been sitting at the bench for a while, listening.

lines.speaker: theo
lines.text: Oh. Sorry. I heard it being tuned and I couldn't help myself. It's a Brandt upright. They don't make them like this.

lines.speaker: theo
lines.text: I'm Theo. I play in the evenings at the harbor hotel, and I've been wandering the lane for a month looking for a piano I liked.

lines.speaker: theo
lines.text: Your gran used to let me practice here after closing. In exchange, I got whatever was left in the custard pot.

lines.speaker: theo
lines.text: Custard cups, crème brûlée, anything with caramel. And if the piano's free on Friday nights, I'd love to play.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Theo is now a regular.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: As the paper lanterns glow, familiar faces come wandering up the lane, each pretending to be passing by.

lines.speaker: gus
lines.text: Lanterns! Haven't seen those lit since your gran's last summer. Saw them from the harbor and had to check.

lines.speaker: edith
lines.text: I taught half this street to sit up straight at a table. Please don't make me prove it. Pass me a cake slice.

lines.speaker: mina
lines.text: I brought flowers for every table! Fine, three tables. The bucket only goes so far.

lines.speaker: dex
lines.text: I'm just here for a quick, unofficial look. Please ignore the notebook. It says "Competitor Terrace: Alarmingly Charming."

lines.speaker: dex
lines.text: Between us, MegaBun's been asking about café terraces. Whole new product line. Something called a "Third Place Experience."

lines.speaker: gus
lines.text: Third place? This is the first place. They can keep their numbers.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A cheer goes up. It's the loudest this terrace has been in years.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The mural is up, the bunting sways. Behind the frame is another folded page, pressed flat, with a pinch of sugar still on it.

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: You found the second one. I knew you would. I'm proud of you, dear.

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: Cake is only a few simple things: sugar, eggs, butter and a bit of nerve. The nerve is the part nobody writes down.

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: Make it for the people who are sitting here, not the people who might someday. They'll taste the difference.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The page goes into the Recipe Book, right beside the first.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Fairy lights on, parasols up, piano in tune. The terrace gate swings wide, and for the first time in years, it doesn't squeak.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: I brought a tiered cake. Three tiers. I know, I know, but it deserved it. Don't tell the pigeons.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Mint's behaving, tomatoes are in, and there's cookies. Best summer I can remember. Don't tell anyone I said so.

lines.speaker: theo
lines.text: Friday night's mine, then. I've been practicing something slow and sweet. It goes well with caramel.

lines.speaker: gus
lines.text: Two places to eat on one street. Gran would've said that was greedy. Then she'd have asked for a third.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A shadow falls across the table. A woman in a very sharp suit studies the terrace through very expensive glasses.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She says nothing. She takes a photo of the cake, a photo of the piano, and a photo of you. Then she leaves.

lines.speaker: dex
lines.text: That's Vice President of Neighborhood Synergy. She doesn't come out for just any bakery. This is... new.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Tucked under a sugar bowl is one last envelope, in loopy handwriting you know by now.

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: Well done again, dear. Now keep your eyes open. Someone has noticed you. That's either very good or very interesting.
